context.title: A Temple Vision Begins
context.summary: Fourteen years after Jerusalem's fall, Ezekiel is taken in vision to a high mountain in Israel, where a bronze-like man with a measuring reed shows him the gates and courts of a new temple.
context.background: The vision is dated about 573 BC (v. 1). Chapters 40–48 are read in different ways: as plans for a literal future temple, as a symbolic picture of God's perfect presence among his people, or as fulfilled in Christ and the church. Either way, Ezekiel receives plans for a holy place never again defiled.

customs.note: Six 'long' cubits, each a standard cubit plus a handbreadth (about 20.5 inches): roughly ten feet.
Each gate had three guard rooms on each side (v. 10), a layout like city gates excavated in Israel, stressing protection of the holy place.

watchFor: 'Declare all that thou seest to the house of Israel' (v. 4).

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4).

events.title: Prophecies of Ezekiel
events.summary: Passage: Ezekiel 1:1–48:35. People: Ezekiel. Lasted about 23 years.
